items.q: During a laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) inguinal hernia repair, placing fixation tacks in the 'Triangle of Pain' lateral to the spermatic vessels risks entrapment and permanent injury to which nerves?
o: Femoral branch of genitofemoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves
items.exp: The Triangle of Pain is bounded medially by testicular vessels, superiorly by the iliopubic tract, and laterally by the anterior superior iliac spine. It transmits the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve, the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN), and the femoral nerve. Fixation tacks placed in this zone cause severe chronic neuropathic pain and burning paresthesia in the anterolateral thigh.
r: Incorrect. Iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves run in the anterior abdominal wall layers.
Correct. Tacks in the Triangle of Pain injure the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve and femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve.
Incorrect. Obturator nerve lies deep in the pelvis below the pectineal line.
Incorrect. Subcostal nerve lies well superior to the inguinal region.
items.kp: Tacks in the Triangle of Pain risk injuring the lateral femoral cutaneous and genitofemoral nerves, causing chronic neuralgia.
